xref.title: Pre-Suicide Activities (1980)
xref.body: In the days leading up to his death, Ian seemed to be in good spirits, with no seizures reported. On Thursday, May 15th, 1980, he played pool with bassist Peter Hook. The next day, Peter dropped Ian off at his parents' house with instructions to pack for the upcoming American tour. On Saturday, May 17th, Ian bailed on plans to water ski with guitarist Barney Sumner, citing a need to rest and wanting to watch a cool movie on TV. "On Thursday May 15th, 1980, Ian hung out with bass player Peter Hook playing pool in a local pub."

xref.title: Intervention and Second Rehab Stint (1994)
xref.body: On March 25th, 1994, an intervention by friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt Cobain to address his self-destructive behavior and heroin addiction. He reluctantly agreed to try rehab again, checking into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on Thursday, March 30th. "On March 25th, 1994, an intervention of friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt that his self-destructive tendencies brought on by his heroin issues had to stop, so he reluctantly and angrily agreed to try rehab again."

xref.title: Antitrust Hearing and Inconclusive Outcome (June 1995)
xref.body: A hearing was scheduled for Thursday, June 30, 1995, in Washington D.C., where members of Pearl Jam's organization and supportive music industry figures presented their case against Ticketmaster. Despite intense media coverage, the government's investigation was closed later in 1995 without any substantial action, with only a promise for continued monitoring of the ticketing industry. "But in the end, nothing came of it. The government investigation was closed in 1995 without anyone doing anything."

xref.title: Disappearance from Courthouse (July 9, 1998)
xref.body: On the morning of Thursday, July 9, 1998, Scott Wyland was last seen smoking cigarettes and answering questions on the steps of the Los Angeles County Courthouse. Upon hearing about the $250,000 arrest warrant, he vanished, knowing he would be arrested if he entered the building. "He knew that he'd be arrested the second he put inside, so he vanished."

xref.title: Jeff Healey's Bar Residency (2001)
xref.body: Following an opening gig for Jeff Healey in Halifax in Summer 2001, Healey invited the band to be the house band at his new Toronto bar, Healey's, on Bathurst and Queen. The Trews accepted, playing every Thursday throughout Summer and Fall 2001. "He said, look, I'm starting a bar called Healey's. You guys give me my house band every Thursday."

xref.title: Final Visit from Mike Starr (April 4, 2002)
xref.body: On Thursday, April 4, 2002, former bandmate Mike Starr visited Lane Staley's condo and was shocked by his emaciated appearance, offering to call 911. Staley vehemently refused, stating he would never speak to Starr again if he did. Starr left feeling angry and discouraged, with Staley pleading, "not like this, don't leave like this." Mike Starr is believed to have been the last person to see Lane Staley alive. "Mike was shocked at how bad Lane looked, an offer to call 911. Lane said, if you do that, I will never talk to you again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Layne Staley's Last Known Interaction (April 4, 2002)
xref.body: On Thursday, April 4, 2002, former Alice in Chains bandmate Mike Starr visited Layne Staley's condo. Starr was shocked by Staley's severely deteriorated appearance and urged him to call 911, but Staley refused. Starr eventually left, feeling angry, discouraged, and sad, telling Staley, "not like this, don't leave like this." Mike Starr is believed to have been the last person to see Layne Staley alive. "Looks like he was the last guy to see Lane alive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death on Tour Bus (December 3, 2015)
xref.body: On December 1, 2015, The Wildabouts played in Toronto. On December 2, Weiland went out late with bassist Tommy Black. The next morning, December 3, Weiland woke around 9 AM on the tour bus, then returned to bed as the bus headed to Medina, Minnesota. When the bus arrived in Bloomington, Tommy Black found Weiland unresponsive and stiff around 8 PM after Weiland's wife, Jamie, requested the tour manager, Aaron Moller, check on him due to an unanswered text. Police pronounced him dead at the scene. "At around 8 pm, local time in Minnesota, Moller found Wyland lying in a fetal position on his left side. His eyes were half closed. His body was stiff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tour Bus Death (December 3, 2015)
xref.body: Scott Weiland died on The Wildabouts' tour bus on December 3, 2015, in Bloomington, Minnesota. He was found unresponsive by the band's tour manager in the back bedroom of the bus. "On Thursday, December 3rd, 2015, The Wild Abuts Tour Bus was in the parking lot of a country in and sweet hotel in Bloomington, Minnesota."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death (2017)
xref.body: Chester Bennington died by suicide via hanging before 9 a.m. Pacific time on Thursday, July 20, 2017. This date also marked Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, with whom Bennington shared a very close bond. Cornell's death was "devastating" to Bennington, as both men battled drugs, alcohol, depression, and the pressures of being in a superstar band, ultimately described as "kindred spirits." "Chester Bennington died by his own hand, a hanging. One time before 9 a.m. Pacific time on Thursday, July 20th."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Discovery of Death (July 20, 2017)
xref.body: On the morning of Thursday, July 20, 2017, at approximately 9 AM, a housekeeper found Chester Bennington hanging from a bedroom door at his house in Palos Verdes Estates. She alerted a driver who had arrived to pick him up for the TV commercial, and the driver subsequently called 911. "At around 9 a.m. on the morning of the 20th, a housekeeper found Chester hanging from a door in the bedroom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: "Get Out of Jail" Party and Heroin Overdose
xref.body: On Thursday, February 1, 1979, Sid Vicious was released from Reikers Island Prison and went to his new girlfriend Michelle Robinson's apartment in Greenwich Village for a "get out of jail party" hosted by his mother Beverly. Despite having just left detox, Sid injected heroin during the party and, after guests left, found and injected another quantity of exceptionally pure heroin (perhaps 80% pure) from his mother's purse, to which his detoxified body was no longer accustomed. His breathing slowed, his heart rate fell, and he died, being found by his mother at sunrise on February 2nd next to drug paraphernalia. "It appears that sometime after Graval left, Sid went into his mother's purse and found another quantity of heroin which he injected." "He went back to bed. His breathing slowed, his heart rate fell, and he died."

xref.title: Date of Death and Cause
xref.body: Chester Bennington, the vocalist for Linkin Park, was confirmed dead by his own hand on Thursday, July 20, 2017. His death came as a shock and was widely considered unexpected, even among a series of other musician deaths around that time. "Chester Bennington, vocalist with Lincoln Park, was not only dead, but dead by his own hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Detailed Drinking Schedule
xref.body: The band The Killers reportedly follows a specific drinking schedule throughout the week. On Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, they drink Absolute Vodka and Maker's Mark Bourbon. On Sunday, they consume Tequila and Jameson's. The remaining days, Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, are reserved for Jack Daniels and Gin, according to Mr. Jeff Fist. "I reported that they drank absolute vodka and Makers Mark Bourbon Monday, Wednesday and Friday, and Tequila and Jamison's on Sunday."

xref.title: Early 2000s Emo Peak and Late 2010s Return
xref.body: My Chemical Romance was a prominent band during Emo's peak in the early 2000s. They "disappeared" by the early 2010s as the genre waned, but returned by the end of the decade, signaling a strong emo revival alongside a new generation of groups exploring the genre. "It had its moments early in the century with bands like Dashboard Conventional and saves the day, Thursday, store the year, taking back Sunday and my chemical romance." "My chemical romance disappeared." "By the end of the decade, my chemical romance was back."

xref.title: Enforced Detoxification
xref.body: After being released on bail in November 1978, Sid Vicious assaulted someone with a smashed beer bottle, leading to his re-arrest and a period of enforced detoxification at Reikers Island Prison, which he completed before his final release. "he was sent to Reikers for a period of enforced detoxification. After completing that rehab, he was released on that Thursday, February 1st."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Gig at Erics Club (Year Unspecified)
xref.body: The band played their inaugural gig at Erics, a renowned basement club in Liverpool where many influential bands like The Clash, Sex Pistols, Devo, Pere Ubu, The Cure, and XTC performed. Erics had an open-door policy on Thursday nights, allowing unpaid members to showcase their music. "We used to go to a club in Liverpool called Erics, which was great. A very famous club."

xref.title: Murder in the Chelsea Hotel
xref.body: Nancy Spungin died in Room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel between 8 and 10 AM on October 12, 1978. She was found in the bathroom under the sink, having been stabbed in the lower abdomen with a Jaguar Wilderness K-11 knife, causing fatal external and internal hemorrhaging. The medical examiner concluded it was murder, not suicide. "It was 10.45 on the morning of Thursday, October 12th, 1978. Sid was in shock, initially in a panic. He confessed, I stabbed her, but I never meant to kill her."

xref.title: Ocean Center Concert (July 17)
xref.body: Robert Palmer performed his "blue-eyed soul" brand of music at the Ocean Center in Daytona Beach on Thursday, July 17, with a showtime of 8 p.m. The event was advertised to include a special guest. "Robert Palmer brings his brand of blue I'd sold the Ocean Center in Daytona Beach Thursday July 17th Showtime for Robert Palmer is 8 p.m."

xref.title: Residency Offer to The Trews
xref.body: Jeff Healey saw The Trews open for him in Halifax in the summer of 2001 and was impressed. He subsequently offered them a weekly residency as the house band at his new establishment, Jeff Healey's bar, on Bathurst and Queen in Toronto, performing every Thursday. "He really liked us. He said, look, I'm starting a bar called Healey's. You guys give me my house band every Thursday."
